blindSummary: Trans visitors face real risk in this country, but the trajectory is surprisingly positive: after briefly criminalising same-sex intimacy in 2019, it decriminalised in 2020, and in November 2024 voters ratified a new constitution that rejected calls to criminalise homosexuality. There is no legal gender recognition; social conservatism persists; but the constitutional debate is now public and the pro-criminalisation side lost.
blindOutOfScope: Formal decriminalisation (2020) and constitution (2024); the social climate lags.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): this country criminalised same-sex intimacy in 2019 (up to 6 months and a large fine), then decriminalised in 2020 after senate approval of repeal - sharply dividing opinion. The November 2024 constitution codified the right to respect for private life but retained a provision limiting marriage to opposite-sex couples. No legal gender recognition.

Anti-criminalisation campaign news platform (Nov 2024): this country's new constitution (ratified by referendum with 90%+ approval) rejected appeals to criminalise homosexuality and included protections for LGBT+ rights, while codifying a marriage definition excluding same-sex couples; civil society had pushed for criminalisation during the drafting under the transitional military regime.

A major foreign government's 2019 human-rights report on this country: official assessment covering the year the new penal code criminalised same-sex conduct - documents the legal change and societal discrimination.

LGBT news site (Dec 2019): this country criminalised homosexuality (up to 6 months' prison, a fine of roughly $8,500) - a country that never had a colonial-era ban; two men had already been arrested and bribed police to be released; a prominent LGBT activist said the law drove the community underground and created harassment.

Overseas LGBT news outlet (July 2020): this country formally decriminalised homosexuality - the national assembly overturned the 2019 ban, restoring the pre-2019 status where same-sex conduct was not criminal.

National news outlet (Oct 2019): analysis of the new penal code (a law of 5 July 2019) - one provision classifies 'sexual relations between people of the same sex' under 'sexual assaults and attacks on morals'; recalls the 2013 controversy when two men celebrating a union were arrested and released because no law then criminalised adults.
blindTangential: The 2020 decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the 2024 constitution rejected criminalisation.
